explanation: At the North Pole the star sits almost overhead, and at the Equator it lies on the horizon. Sailors used it to find their latitude at night.

claims.text: In the Northern Hemisphere, the angle of Polaris above the horizon roughly equals the observer's latitude.
The height of Polaris stays roughly the same through the night and through the year, and it does not change with longitude.
Polaris appears almost overhead at the North Pole and on the horizon at the Equator.
Navigators used the height of Polaris to find their latitude at night.
